title: Barcelona vs. Real Madrid Player Ratings: Mbappe Hits 100 As Los Blancos Stun Camp Nou
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath6:43 PM EDTThe night was all about Kylian Mbappé. / David Ramos/Getty ImagesReal Madrid put themselves right back into the La Liga title race with a stunning 2–1 win over Barcelona at Camp Nou on Sunday night.
In a match in which six Ballon d’Or nominees started, it was Kylian Mbappé who stole the headlines with his match-winning double, though the performance was as much about José Mourinho as any player.

As expected, Barça dominated the possession, but they struggled to break down their opponents, while Madrid got an unexpected breakthrough five minutes before half-time as Gerard Martín’s attempted clearance cannoned back off Mbappé and into the goal.

The hosts fought back after the interval with Raphinha’s equalizer and pushed frantically for a winner that never came. Instead, it was Madrid who came away with bragging rights and renewed hope as a superb late counterattack ended up at the feet of Mbappé, who tapped into an open net to silence the Camp Nou and dramatically change the narrative in La Liga this season.

It was a classic Mourinho performance. / Alberto Gardin/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesThe last time these two met, Barcelona ran out winners to officially confirm their La Liga title at the end of last season.

This time around—though neither manager would publicly admit it—the state of play prior to kick-off meant that a win for Barcelona would essentially end a floundering Real Madrid’s title hopes even before Halloween.
With Mbappé’s bizarre point-blank ricochet and late tap-in—his 99th and 100th goals for Real Madrid—Los Blancos are very much still alive and kicking in the race.

Barcelona did not face the same team that struggled to cope in the Madrid derby prior to the international break. Instead, the host came up against what felt like the archetypal, teak-tough, counter-heavy Mourinho side, only too delighted to play the role of party poopers. Hansi Flick’s team didn’t seem to know quite what to do with Madrid’s competence.
It’s a result that changes everything. Barça no longer look unstoppable, and Madrid are very much back.
Raphinha scored his 13th of the season. /  Lluis GENE/AFP/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Joan García—7.2: Made three saves on the night but nothing he could’ve have done about the first goal.
RB: Xavi Espart—6.2: Espart’s first Clásico lasted just half and hour, with the teenager trudging off after feeling the lasting effects of a heavy challenge from Aurélien Tchouaméni.
CB: Pau Cubarsí—6.3: Struggled in his duels and will be unhappy at how he was played around on the counter at times.
CB: Gerard Martín—6.3: In hindsight, it was a poor decision to clear a cross—without pressure—straight into the onrushing shins of the world’s best striker.
LB: João Cancelo—7.7: Started at left back and ended on the right, the Portugal international was effective in creating chances and did well in his battles with Yan Diomande.
CM: Rodri—6.9: Missed midweek, Rodri asserted control but not creativity here with Barça somewhat lacking.

CM: Pedri—7.7: As against PSG, he looked a soft touch in the first half, failing to win his duels and uncharacteristically sloppy in possession. A delicious disguised assist for Raphinha’s equalizer largely made up for all previous sins.
RW: Lamine Yamal—6.9: Off the pace. The Ballon d’Or contender skewed a gift of a chance to equalize right before half time and was ultimately outshone by the stone-cold Mbappé.
AM: Fermín López—6.3: A frustrating night for López, who was unable to affect the game against Madrid’s solid midfield.
